context: 1M-point WebGL scatterplot with 6 synthetic Gaussian clusters, interactive brush selection, and an inset 2D histogram of the brushed subset
first_impression: Technically impressive performance demo with honest encoding choices throughout — data-driven scale domains, colorblind-safe palette, and no size-encoding deception.
what_works: X/Y scales use d3.min/d3.max with .nice() for data-driven domains; inset histogram color scale uses data-driven maxCount from d3.max(grid), not a hardcoded ceiling.
what_doesnt: Inset histogram uses a hardcoded 20x20 bin grid regardless of brushed selection size (should apply Sturges' or Scott's rule to brushedCount); pixel positions are precomputed once at init so the chart cannot adapt if scales were to update dynamically.
